one_liner: LGPL C audio resampler (the SoX engine) that ran 6.8-22x libsamplerate 0.2.2's throughput in a third-party streaming benchmark.
what_it_does: Converts PCM audio between any constant rational or irrational pair of sample rates, with an optional variable-rate mode (SOXR_VR, soxr_set_io_ratio with a slew length). The native API is soxr_create(in_rate, out_rate, channels, ...) followed by soxr_process() or a pull-style soxr_output() with an input callback, plus soxr_oneshot() for buffers held in memory. I/O can be float32, float64, int32 or int16, interleaved or split per channel, with gain and optional TPDF dither to int16. Quality is a recipe (QQ, LQ, MQ, HQ = 20-bit, VHQ = 28-bit) or explicit precision (15-33 bits), passband end, stopband start and phase response (linear, intermediate or minimum).
how_it_is_fast: The README says the design follows Laurent de Soras' 'The Quest For The Perfect Resampler': Julius O. Smith's bandlimited interpolation combined with FFT-based oversampling. In cr.c a long, steep low-pass runs as overlap-save FFT convolution in large blocks (DFT sizes from 2^10 up to 2^17 by default). For the benchmarked near-unity ratio that block upsamples 2x, then a short polyphase FIR with polynomial-interpolated coefficients produces the fractional step, sized to a 400 kB coefficient budget. Rational ratios with small factors skip the coefficient interpolation, and power-of-two factors use half-band stages. CPUID at run time picks the SIMD engines on x86: HQ runs single precision with SSE and PFFFT (cr32s), and VHQ runs double precision with AVX and PFFFT (cr64s). libsamplerate instead does a per-sample time-domain sinc convolution.
when_to_use: Offline or batch conversion at real ratios (44.1 to 48 kHz, 96 to 44.1 kHz, downsampling for ML front ends). python-soxr's README times 10 s of 48 to 44.1 kHz at 10.8 ms for soxr HQ against 223 ms for libsamplerate sinc_medium, and 14.5 ms for VHQ against 794 ms for sinc_best.

Replacing libsamplerate SINC_MEDIUM or SINC_BEST in throughput-bound desktop or server code that can absorb about 10-20 ms of filter delay. In the third-party table HQ gets 52.9 vs 4.8 Mframes/s on stereo, and VHQ gets 32.1 vs 1.6 for BEST.
Mixed-format pipelines that want one call to deinterleave, convert int16/int32/float64 to the engine's type, resample, apply gain and dither back to int16.
Multichannel streams on spare cores: with num_threads = 0 and an OpenMP build, soxr processes channels in parallel (the default is 1 thread).
Applications that need tunable quality, e.g. minimum-phase filters for lower pre-ringing, or 28-33-bit precision for mastering.
when_not_to_use: Live monitoring or other paths with a 1-2 ms budget. In the SampleRateTap measurement HQ holds back 424-788 frames (8.8-16.4 ms at 48 kHz) and VHQ 433 frames. The README itself quotes about 1000 output samples (about 20 ms) for HQ at 44.1/48 kHz. libsamplerate MEDIUM holds 46 frames and SampleRateTap 24.

Upstream builds on AArch64 (Apple silicon, Graviton). FindSIMD32.cmake tries NEON flags only when the processor name starts with 'arm', and SSE flags otherwise, so 0.1.3 builds its scalar engines there. The dofuuz/soxr fork says it enables AArch64 optimization for an over 2x speed-up.
Closed-source products that must link statically and cannot meet LGPL-2.1 relinking terms. r8brain-free-src is MIT and header-only.

Projects that need a maintained upstream. The last release is 0.1.3 (2018-02-24). The GitHub mirror has 9 open issues and 6 open pull requests, including a distortion fix (PR #12, 2023), AArch64 support (PR #9, 2022) and a CMake minimum bump (issue #14) that newer CMake needs.
Real clock-drift correction. soxr has a variable-rate mode but no ratio estimation, so an external servo must feed soxr_set_io_ratio. SampleRateTap recovers the clock itself.

integration.form: shared lib (static via -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF); optional libsoxr-lsr with a libsamplerate-style API
integration.dependencies: none required beyond libm. Optional: OpenMP (multi-channel threading and the FFT-cache locks), the bundled PFFFT (BSD-like licence, on by default for the HQ SIMD engine), libavcodec as an alternative FFT, and libavutil for NEON detection on 32-bit ARM
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler with 64-bit integers; the library builds as -std=gnu89; CMake 3.1 per CMakeLists.txt (INSTALL says 3.0). CMake 4.x needs a minimum-version bump (issue #14; fixed in the dofuuz fork).
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 with run-time selection between SSE (HQ) and AVX (VHQ) engines; 32-bit ARM NEON when libavutil is found or SOXR_USE_SIMD is set; scalar elsewhere, including AArch64 in upstream 0.1.3; Windows (MSVC, MinGW), Linux, macOS
integration.thread_safety: One soxr_t per stream; concurrent calls on the same object are not documented as safe. The process-wide Ooura FFT table (fft4g_cache.h) is guarded by an OpenMP readers-writer lock that compiles to no-ops in builds without OpenMP (ccrw2.h). That table serves minimum- and intermediate-phase filter design and the non-SIMD engines.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: soxr-lsr.h and libsoxr-lsr implement the libsamplerate API (src_new, src_process, src_callback_new/read, src_simple, src_set_ratio) for float samples, mapping SRC_SINC_* to soxr's LSR quality recipes. The README says this is not a full emulation and exposes only some of soxr's features.

gotchas: Integer output is risky in 0.1.3. The int16/int32 RINT_CLIP path tests fe_test_invalid() and writes a full-scale clip value when the FE_INVALID flag is set. Issue #11 and PR #12 (open since 2023-11) report a stale flag corrupting otherwise valid samples. The float32 output path used in the benchmark does not go through this check.

int16 output is dithered with a seed built from time(0) and the object's address (soxr.c), so results differ from run to run (issue #8, open). The dofuuz fork makes int16 output reproducible and fixes a periodic-zeros dithering bug.

soxr_oneshot() defaults to LQ quality, not the HQ default of soxr_create(), so pass an explicit quality spec. Streaming calls return a varying number of output frames, and soxr_delay() changes with the streaming state.

Environment variables override the application's runtime spec: SOXR_NUM_THREADS, SOXR_COEFS_SIZE, SOXR_MIN_DFT_SIZE, SOXR_LARGE_DFT_SIZE and SOXR_USE_SIMD/SIMD32/SIMD64. Pin or clear them in benchmarks and deployments.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick soxr over r8brain-free-src for raw throughput when LGPL is acceptable: in the same SampleRateTap table it is 3.1-3.2x faster at the 120 dB tier and 1.7-2.3x faster at the 140 dB tier, with less delay than r8brain's default settings (VHQ 433 frames vs 1,700-1,782), all derived from page data. Pick r8brain for an MIT, header-only drop-in. LibFResample's numbers come from a different harness (libsamplerate 0.1.8 on a Phenom II), and zita-resampler (GPL) has only directional claims, so neither can be compared with soxr directly.
verified_claims_summary: The SampleRateTap author's harness (bench_compare.cpp, Google Benchmark, GCC 13.3 -O3, Ubuntu 24.04 packages soxr 0.1.3 and libsamplerate 0.2.2, unnamed shared Xeon at 2.10 GHz, median of 5, 2026-09-25) streams a float32 interleaved 997 Hz sine from 48 kHz to 48 kHz x (1 + 200 ppm) in 128-frame blocks, single-threaded, counting output frames. soxr HQ vs libsamplerate MEDIUM: 114.3 vs 5.2 (mono), 52.9 vs 4.8 (stereo) and 12.9 vs 1.9 (8-ch) Mframes/s; soxr VHQ vs BEST: 32.1 vs 1.6 (stereo). That is about 6.8-22x, derived from page data. Reading the harness found no flaw: soxr reads input in place while libsamplerate gets an extra 128-frame copy, which is negligible at these rates. The page's THD+N measurement covers VHQ (at the 24-bit format ceiling) but not HQ, so the HQ-to-MEDIUM quality pairing rests on vendor-stated stopbands.
status_note: Upstream has been abandoned since 0.1.3 (2018-02-24), but that release is still what Linux distributions ship, and the LGPL-2.1-or-later C sources build with CMake. For ARM64, CMake 4 or reproducible int16 output, use the maintained dofuuz/soxr fork (last commit 2026-06-27), which python-soxr bundles.
